description: 660 litre four-castor plastic refuse container with a domed hinged lid, standing behind convenience stores and condos

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Large rectangular moulded plastic wheelie bin, a four-sided box-shaped tub clearly wider than it is tall and flat-sided, not round, its four flat panels tapering slightly inward toward the base with broad shallow ribs moulded down them and a moulded grip rail running along the back below the rim, closed by one wide flat rectangular lid hinged along the back top edge and overhanging the front rim as a thick lip, and underneath four swivel castors on short square pedestals, one at each corner, each castor a solid wheel in a plain U-shaped fork Materials: Dark green polyethylene chalky and sun-bleached across the lid and the upper front panel, grey and black scuffs along both ends where it has been dragged, dark grease and leachate staining down the front below the rim and pooled around the castor pedestals, a faded white stencilled panel on the front.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 1,228/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.94 x 1.22 x 0.78 m exactly (the first build ran 1.044 wide and 1.228 tall). Proxy band table: every body band within 0.03 H in width; band 0 (the castor span) taken from -0.076 to within 0.02 by moving the castors to x +-0.35, z +-0.20 off the proxy's 0.614 x 0.384 H span. Body frustum 0.80 x 0.66 -> 0.90 x 0.74 from the proxy occupancy (0.84 -> 0.94 W over 0.14-0.86 H).
featureReviews.notes: Depth reads +0.06 H deeper than the proxy on every band: the declared 0.78 m is kept because the asset notes derive 0.79 from the plate's own yaw solve, and a single-view proxy hallucinates the rear.

featureReviews.evidence: A HIPPED lid: slab over the rim, a 0.88 x 0.72 -> 0.50 x 0.40 dome frustum 75 mm tall, a raised 0.30 x 0.22 panel on top, twenty vent slots on the two long slopes tilted to the slope angle, three knuckles down the -X edge with two mates on the rim, and the lid-hinge pivot on that edge about Z. The first build was a flat slab with corner tabs and its hinge along the rear.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's lid has rounded plan corners and a moulded rectangle inside the panel; neither is authored.

featureReviews.evidence: Four swivel castors as real assemblies -- tyre r 0.07 x 0.038, zinc hub disc, fork, swivel plate and pin -- where the first build had black blocks; five front ribs 75 mm wide and 30 mm proud in a lighter crown tone, where the first build's were the body tone and read as flat. Grime canvas mapped once over the body height after a 0.60 m repeat left a hard wash band mid-body.
featureReviews.notes: Ribs are boxes, not the plate's rounded profile; at prop distance the crown tone carries the read.

notes: WIDTH CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from 1.37 m to 0.94 m; depth and height are unchanged at 0.78 and 1.22. The 1.37 was a list-time estimate and it made the bin half again as wide as it should be against its own depth. Two independent readings agree and neither is the declaration. The Meshy proxy's band table read width/height 0.65-0.76 across bands 2-9 against the build's 0.94-1.09 -- eight of ten bands over the 0.12 flag, mean |delta width| 0.34 -- while reading DEPTH at 0.50-0.62 against the build's 0.55-0.64, which was already right; an error in one axis only is a declaration error rather than a scale one. And the plate, read as a 3/4 view at roughly 30 degrees yaw, puts the front face at ~620 px and the side at ~300, so true width/depth is (620/cos30)/(300/sin30) = 1.19 against the proxy's 1.23 and the build's 1.76. After the correction the band table reads mean |delta width| 0.0235 with no band over the flag.
